CVX.rationale: Chevron's Q1 2026 results reveal a sharp deterioration in profitability: EPS fell 44.5% YoY to $1.11 (from $2.00), net income declined 34.7%, and operating cash flow dropped 51.6% to $2.51B. The company is trading at a P/E of 33.67x—more than double its 1-year  of of near thex low of5x)—at the top of its 365-day range (15.1–34.8). This extreme valuation expansion has occurred despite worsening fundamentals: net margin compressedpressed to 5.9% (from 7.8% a year ago), ROE fell to 5.9% (from 10.5%), and the balance sheet shows rising liabilities (+$33.8B since Q1 2025) with equity only growing modestly. The Q1 results were distorted by ~$3B in unfavorable timing effects (legal reserves, FX), but even adjusted EPS of $1.41 was well below the prior year's $2.15. Oil prices at ~$100/bbl should be supportive, yet Chevron's earnings power is clearly impaired relative to what the market is pricing. The stock has rallied 24% from its Aug 2025 low of $153 to $191, fully pricing in the geopolitical oil premium while the underlying business is generating. There is no near-term fundamental catalyst to justify re-rating higher; the next earnings event is July 31, and management explicitly stated they are not changing capital allocation despite elevated prices. Risks include potential Iran deal (oil price collapse), California regulatory scrutiny on refining margins, and the unresolved Hess arbitration. The combination of deteriorating fundamentals, extreme valuation vs. history, and absence of positive catalysts makes this strongly unattractive.
